Cooling Test

A closed-loop cooling system for a laser machine was tested on a test bench. The pump circulated water through a filter and a heat exchanger, after which it returned to the reservoir. At a flow rate of 18 liters per minute, the outlet temperature remained at 27 degrees. This is the result of a laboratory test, not a guarantee of the same temperature under any load. The operator recorded the readings every five minutes and did not change the settings during the test series.

After replacing the filter, the pressure before the heat exchanger decreased, but the flow rate remained the same. Engineer Anna suspected that some of the water was passing through the bypass valve. She asked the technician to close it only temporarily. The technician complied, but then returned the valve to its original position: leaving it closed when the pump was off was prohibited. No signs of leaks were found at the connections.

The second session lasted 45 minutes. The sensor on the return line initially showed a temperature spike, although two control thermometers did not confirm it. This spike should not be considered evidence of overheating. After checking the cable, the sensor's readings matched those of the control thermometers. Anna suggested replacing the connector while keeping the sensor itself for now; the supervisor agreed to this sequence of actions.

The report must distinguish between water flow and electricity consumption. The pump consumed 240 watts, but this figure alone cannot be used to calculate the water volume without additional data. The next test is scheduled for June 14, with a backup date of June 17. If the new connector is not delivered on time, the test date will be changed, not the pump. The client will only receive the verified results from both test series.
